{{Short description|SIMD instruction set}}
'''Supplemental Streaming SIMD Extensions 3''' ('''SSSE3''' or '''SSE3S''') is a [[SIMD]] instruction set created by [[Intel]] and is the fourth iteration of the [[Streaming SIMD Extensions|SSE]] technology.

== History ==
SSSE3 was first introduced with Intel processors based on the [[Intel Core (microarchitecture)|Core microarchitecture]] on June 26, 2006 with the "Woodcrest" Xeons.

SSSE3 has been referred to by the codenames '''[[Tejas and Jayhawk|Tejas]] New Instructions (TNI)''' or '''[[Intel Core 2#Merom|Merom]] New Instructions (MNI)''' for the first processor designs intended to support it.

SSSE3 has enhanced for HD audio/video decoding/encoding, for example [[Advanced Audio Coding|AAC]].

== Functionality == 
SSSE3 contains 16 new discrete instructions. Each instruction can act on 64-bit MMX or 128-bit XMM registers. Therefore, Intel's materials refer to 32 new instructions. They include:<ref name=":0">{{cite tech report |url=https://www.intel.com/content/dam/www/public/us/en/documents/manuals/64-ia-32-architectures-optimization-manual.pdf#G3.1106470 |title=Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Optimization Reference Manual |year=2016 |access-date=June 22, 2018 |pages=92-93 |section=2.9.5 |publisher=Intel.com |archive-date=June 20, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180620123843/https://www.intel.com/content/dam/www/public/us/en/documents/manuals/64-ia-32-architectures-optimization-manual.pdf#G3.1106470 |url-status=live }}</ref>

* Twelve instructions that perform horizontal addition or subtraction operations.
* Six instructions that evaluate absolute values.
* Two instructions that perform multiply-and-add operations and speed up the evaluation of [[dot product]]s.
* Two instructions that accelerate packed integer multiply operations and produce integer values with scaling.
* Two instructions that perform a byte-wise, in-place shuffle according to the second shuffle control operand.
* Six instructions that negate packed integers in the destination operand if the corresponding element in the source operand is negative.
* Two instructions that align data from the composite of two operands.

==New instructions==

In the table below, {{math|''satsw''(X)}} (read as 'saturate to signed word') takes a signed integer X, and converts it to −32768 if it is less than −32768, to +32767 if it is greater than 32767, and leaves it unchanged otherwise. As normal for the Intel architecture, bytes are 8 bits, words 16 bits, and dwords 32 bits; 'register' refers to an MMX or XMM vector register.<ref name=":0" />

{| class="wikitable plainrowheaders"
|-
! scope="col" | Instruction
! scope="col" | Definition
! scope="col" | Explanation
|-
! scope="row" | <code>PSIGNB</code>, <code>PSIGNW</code>, <code>PSIGND</code>
| Packed Sign
| Negate the elements of a register of bytes, words or dwords if the sign of the corresponding elements of another register is negative.
|-
! scope="row" | <code>PABSB</code>, <code>PABSW</code>, <code>PABSD</code>
| Packed Absolute Value
| Fill the elements of a register of bytes, words or dwords with the absolute values of the elements of another register
|-
! scope="row" | <code>PALIGNR</code>
| Packed Align Right
| take two registers, concatenate their values, and pull out a register-length section from an offset given by an immediate value encoded in the instruction.
|- 
! scope="row" | <code>PSHUFB</code>
| Packed Shuffle Bytes
| takes registers of bytes A = [a<sub>0</sub> a<sub>1</sub> a<sub>2</sub> ...] and B = [b<sub>0</sub> b<sub>1</sub> b<sub>2</sub> ...] and replaces A with [a<sub>b0</sub> a<sub>b1</sub> a<sub>b2</sub> ...]; except that it replaces the ith entry with 0 if the top bit of b<sub>i</sub> is set.
|-
! scope="row" | <code>PMULHRSW</code>
| Packed Multiply High with Round and Scale
| treat the 16-bit words in registers A and B as signed 16-bit fixed-point numbers between −1.00000000 and +0.99996948... (e.g. 0x4000 is treated as +0.5 and 0xA000 as −0.75), and multiply them together with correct rounding.
|-
! scope="row" | <code>PMADDUBSW</code>
| Multiply and Add Packed Signed and Unsigned Bytes
| Take the bytes in registers A and B, multiply them together, add pairs, signed-saturate and store.  I.e. [a<sub>0</sub> a<sub>1</sub> a<sub>2</sub> ...] <code>PMADDUBSW</code> [b<sub>0</sub> b<sub>1</sub> b<sub>2</sub> ...] = [{{math|''satsw''(a<sub>0</sub>b<sub>0</sub> + a<sub>1</sub>b<sub>1</sub>) ''satsw''(a<sub>2</sub>b<sub>2</sub> + a<sub>3</sub>b<sub>3</sub>) ...}}]
|-
! scope="row" | <code>PHSUBW</code>, <code>PHSUBD</code>
| Packed Horizontal Subtract (Words or Doublewords)
| takes registers A = [a<sub>0</sub> a<sub>1</sub> a<sub>2</sub> ...] and B = [b<sub>0</sub> b<sub>1</sub> b<sub>2</sub> ...] and outputs [a<sub>0</sub>−a<sub>1</sub> a<sub>2</sub>−a<sub>3</sub> ... b<sub>0</sub>−b<sub>1</sub> b<sub>2</sub>−b<sub>3</sub> ...]
|-
! scope="row" | <code>PHSUBSW</code>
| Packed Horizontal Subtract and Saturate Words 
| like PHSUBW, but outputs [{{math|''satsw''(a<sub>0</sub>−a<sub>1</sub>) ''satsw''(a<sub>2</sub>−a<sub>3</sub>) ... ''satsw''(b<sub>0</sub>−b<sub>1</sub>) ''satsw''(b<sub>2</sub>−b<sub>3</sub>) ...}}]
|-
! scope="row" | <code>PHADDW</code>, <code>PHADDD</code>
| Packed Horizontal Add (Words or Doublewords)
| takes registers A = [a<sub>0</sub> a<sub>1</sub> a<sub>2</sub> ...] and B = [b<sub>0</sub> b<sub>1</sub> b<sub>2</sub> ...] and outputs [a<sub>0</sub>+a<sub>1</sub> a<sub>2</sub>+a<sub>3</sub> ... b<sub>0</sub>+b<sub>1</sub> b<sub>2</sub>+b<sub>3</sub> ...]
|-
! scope="row" | <code>PHADDSW</code>
| Packed Horizontal Add and Saturate Words
| like PHADDW, but outputs [{{math|''satsw''(a<sub>0</sub>+a<sub>1</sub>) ''satsw''(a<sub>2</sub>+a<sub>3</sub>) ... ''satsw''(b<sub>0</sub>+b<sub>1</sub>) ''satsw''(b<sub>2</sub>+b<sub>3</sub>) ...}}]
|}
